statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail; moreover, r is true if and only if n is an Armstrong number. Here n is an Armstrong number exactly when, letting k be the unique positive integer with 10^(k-1) <= n < 10^k and defining d_i = (n / 10^i) mod 10 for 0 <= i < k using integer division, one has n = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} d_i^k. In particular, r is false exactly when this equality does not hold.
The function returns a result, either true or false, and does not fail through panic, arithmetic overflow, or out-of-bounds access.

preconditions: There exists an integer k with 1 <= k <= 8 such that n = 10^k.

statement: Whenever the function returns true, letting k be the number of decimal digits of n, one has n <= k * 9^k.
